script.style: Full-colour, approachable Indian slice-of-life manga. Clean confident line art with varied line weight, soft flat cel shading, warm natural daylight, restrained blue and teal accents, simple readable backgrounds. Expressive but natural faces, precise hands. No photorealism, no glossy gradients, no surface microtexture. Absolutely no text, letters, logos, numbers, speech bubbles or captions inside the artwork; device screens show only abstract blank blocks and simple icons.
script.continuity: Keep Dr. Ananya, Meera, Ravi, the Nurse, Mr. Raman and Priya identical to their canonical reference sheets in face traits, hair, build, skin tone and clothing for the whole comic. Device screens never show readable text or real personal data. Page 7 panels 2-3 (07-2, 07-3) are a future vision: soft pale-blue vignette border and lighter, airy palette so they never read as current features.

pages.scan: Opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-05.png with Read. It loaded: 4 panels with no numbers (wide top, two in the middle row, wide bottom).
pages.observation: How I read it: P1: Ananya (left) says 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' Ravi is at the right. P2 (middle left): Ravi says 'I've been feeling tired lately.' The balloon is at top-left and its tail points right to Ravi's face box. Ananya shows only as a dot at the left edge, with no face box. P3 (middle right): narration 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' Ananya's face box is in the centre and Ravi is a dot at the far right edge. P4 (bottom): Ananya says 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' Ravi is at the right. Issues: (1) In P1 and P4, Ananya's balloon sits directly against the right side of her face box with a tiny tail. It covers her name label ('anany', 'ana..') and probably the right edge of her face. Move each balloon off the face. (2) In P4 the balloon sits between Ananya and Ravi. Because the tail is so short, the speaker could be read either way. (3) In P2 the balloon sits on Ananya's side (left) but belongs to Ravi (right). Placing the speaker's balloon over the listener's side can mislead, although the tail does resolve it. (4) The caption box in P3 overlaps the panel's top-left border. (5) Narrative: Ravi says he is tired, and Ananya's only spoken reply is a generic promise. P3 is a narration beat that puts a slogan in place of any visible response (nod, follow-up question). The consultation feels thin, and a reader may want one concrete follow-up. (6) 'Technology' in P3 refers to nothing visible in this scene unless the art shows a screen.
